table.name: concert
table.purpose: One row per concert/show episode (e.g. of a TV singing competition like The X Factor), identifying the concert, its theme/week, the song performed, the venue (stadium), and the year.

col_001.name: concert_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the concert table; unique integer identifier for each concert. Referenced by singer_in_concert.

col_002.name: concert_name
col_002.description: Name/theme of the concert or show stage, e.g. 'Auditions', 'Home Visits', 'Super bootcamp', 'Week 1', 'Week 2' — stages of a singing competition.

col_003.name: theme_or_song
col_003.description: Song or theme performed at the concert, e.g. 'Bleeding Love', 'Wide Awake', 'Happy Tonight', 'Free choice'. Could be the concert's theme rather than a specific song; both readings fit.

col_004.name: stadium_id
col_004.description: Foreign key to stadium.col_001; the venue where the concert took place (lookup labels are football club/stadium names like 'Ayr United', 'Brechin City').

col_005.name: year
col_005.description: Year the concert took place (2014 or 2015).

table.name: singer
table.purpose: Directory of singers, each with name, country, song title, release year, age, and a flag (likely whether the singer is male). Referenced by singer_in_concert, which links singers to concerts.

col_001.name: singer_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique integer identifying each singer. Referenced by singer_in_concert.

col_004.name: song_name
col_004.description: Title of a song associated with the singer (e.g. 'Hey Oh', 'Gentleman').

col_005.name: song_release_year
col_005.description: Year the song was released (1992-2016), stored as text.

col_007.name: is_male
col_007.description: Boolean flag stored as 'T'/'F'. Plausibly indicates the singer is male (T=4, F=2); could also be another yes/no attribute, so tentative.

table.name: singer_in_concert
table.purpose: Junction (association) table linking singers to the concerts they perform in; each row states that a given singer performed in a given concert. The composite of both columns likely forms the primary key, though neither column is individually unique (uniqueness 0.5-0.6, no single-column PK detected).

col_001.name: singer_id
col_001.description: Identifier of the singer performing in the concert. References singer.col_001 (many_to_one); lookup pairs show singer names (Joe Sharp, Justin Brown, Rose White, etc.). It also statistically joins to concert.col_001, but that is coincidental overlap of small integer IDs, not a real relationship.

col_002.name: concert_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the concert the singer performs in. References concert.col_001 (many_to_one); lookup pairs show concert names (Auditions, Home Visits, Week 1, Week 2). Joins to singer and stadium are coincidental integer overlap, not real relationships. Declared VARCHAR but values are integers.

table.name: stadium
table.purpose: One row per football stadium (Scottish clubs), with capacity and attendance statistics. Referenced by concert and singer_in_concert, which place concerts at these venues.

col_001.name: stadium_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique identifier of the stadium, referenced by concert.col_004 and singer_in_concert.col_002.

col_002.name: team
col_002.description: Name of the football club / team that uses the stadium (e.g. Ayr United, Queen's Park).

col_003.name: stadium_name
col_003.description: Name of the stadium (e.g. Hampden Park, Somerset Park).

col_004.name: capacity
col_004.description: Stadium seating capacity in number of people (2,000 to 52,500; Hampden Park's 52,500 confirms this reading).

col_005.name: highest_attendance
col_005.description: Highest recorded attendance at the stadium (780 to 4,812).

col_006.name: lowest_attendance
col_006.description: Lowest recorded attendance at the stadium (315 to 1,294); consistently the smallest of the three attendance figures per row.

col_007.name: average_attendance
col_007.description: Average attendance at the stadium (552 to 2,106); lies between the lowest and highest figures in each row.
